title: Edge connection pool TLS session resumption causes tenant context bleed during Dedicated peering
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: A high-severity customer escalation reported that during a short peering flapping window, requests from one tenant occasionally received responses containing another tenant's internal hostnames and metadata. Impact: potential exposure of tenant-internal hostnames and transient request misrouting for Dedicated deployments. Observed in production on dedicated-edge nodes handling VPC peering routes between regions.

Symptoms and reproducibility: Intermittent (~0.02% of requests during events) cross-tenant response payloads with DNS names or headers belonging to other tenants. Reproducible when: 1) peering routes are rebalanced (brief TCP connection churn), 2) TLS session resumption is enabled on the edge connection pool, and 3) connection pooling reassigns an idle socket to a new logical request before full tenant context rebind.

Root cause: The edge HTTP/TCP connection pool keyed connections by upstream host and port plus TLS server_name, but did not include the tenant's logical context (tenant_id/connection-namespace) in the pool key. When TLS session resumption reused a socket after a peering reparent, the socket carried cached upstream resolver state and SNAT mapping that could be interpreted under a different tenant's request path. In short: connection reuse without tenant scoping allowed stale per-connection state (resolver response cache, socket-level metadata) to be observed by a different tenant's request during rare race windows.

Short-term mitigations applied: 1) rolled out a targeted config flag (edge.disable_connection_reuse_without_tenant = true) to all Dedicated-edge pools serving affected customers to force per-tenant connection affinity; 2) temporarily disabled TLS session resumption on peered resolver destinations for the most impacted region; 3) communicated a mitigation update to the escalated customer and enabled increased logging for affected nodes. Mitigations reduced incidents to zero for the customer while we prepared the code fix.

Permanent fix implemented: Patch submitted that: (a) expands the connection pool key to include tenant_id and connection-namespace, (b) marks sockets carrying tenant-scoped cache/resolver state as "exclusive" and prevents reuse across tenants, and (c) adds a fast-path check that rejects connection assignment if the connection's cached metadata timestamp is older than the tenant's current routing epoch. The fix also includes unit and integration tests that simulate peering reparent + pool churn.

Rollout plan: Canary deploy to 10% of Dedicated-edge fleet for 48 hours (monitoring: cross-tenant payload rate, 5xx/timeout spikes, TLS handshake rates). If stable, ramp to 50% over 24 hours, then 100% in 72 hours. Post-rollout verification includes synthetic multi-tenant stress tests across peering changes and a customer validation window with the originally impacted tenant.

Postmortem actions and follow-ups: 1) security review and threat analysis to confirm no persistent data exfiltration occurred (completed, low risk); 2) add invariant checks in telemetry to alert on any payloads containing hostnames not belonging to request tenant; 3) audit other pooling codepaths (HTTP/2 connection reuse, gRPC keepalive) for similar missing-tenant scoping; 4) update runbooks to include immediate flag toggles and customer communication templates for future peering-induced churn; 5) upstream internal doc to product and solutions teams describing the subtle coupling between TLS session reuse and tenant-scoped state.

Related artifacts and links: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge/pull/9472; Canary dashboard: https://grafana.internal.redwood/d/edge/tenant-isolation-canary; Incident notes: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/INC/2026-02-26+-+Dedicated+peering+tenant+context+bleed; Customer notification thread: https://gmail.redwood.com/thread/CA+CustomerEsc+12345

Notes: This ticket originated from a customer escalation on 2026-02-26. The fix is non-invasive to hosted API users but important for Dedicated/Private deployments where tenant isolation is a hard requirement.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy two tenants A and B into Dedicated-edge nodes with VPC peering between their VPCs.
2) Enable heavy short-lived flows and configure resolver-forwarding such that resolver responses are cached at socket level (mirror production peering behavior).
3) Trigger peering route reparenting (simulate flapping) while TLS session resumption and connection pooling are enabled.
4) Observe that under pool churn, some requests from tenant A return payloads containing hostnames/metadata associated with tenant B (rare, timing-dependent).
acceptance_criteria: All Dedicated-edge nodes include tenant_id in connection pool key and prevent cross-tenant socket reuse.
No customer-reported cross-tenant payload incidents for 7 days post-rollout.
New invariant alert fires if any response contains hostnames not assigned to the request tenant.
Automated tests cover simulated peering reparent + reuse race windows.
Security review completed and ticket linked to compliance audit.
